McLaren.summary: McLaren has reshaped the side‑pod inlets, engine cover and cooling louvers to tidy up the airflow, while new floor‑edge, diffuser and rear‑suspension fairings add extra grip and keep the car cool on the specific circuit. An alternate rear‑wing flap setting also trims drag for a stronger straight‑line run, meaning the car should be quicker through the corners and on the straights this weekend.

Red Bull Racing.summary: Red Bull’s RB‑19 gets a fresh set of aerodynamic tweaks – the floor and rear diffuser have been reshaped, the side‑pod edge has been nudged, and the mirrors and halo now have smoother fairings – while the cooling vents have been re‑worked to keep the engine happy. All of these changes tighten the car’s airflow and improve cooling, giving the team a better balance and more grip as they chase another win this weekend.

Williams Racing.summary: Williams have rolled out a fresh floor package with new leading‑edge pieces and reshaped corners, giving the car more grip and a cleaner airflow under the car. To match that, they’ve tweaked the rear‑end geometry, re‑profiled the front and rear brake‑ducts and adjusted the rear‑suspension cladding, all to keep the tyres in the optimal temperature window and improve stability through this weekend’s high‑speed corners.

Racing Bulls / RB.summary: Racing Bulls has rolled out a fresh front‑wing package, a re‑shaped brake‑duct/front‑lip combo and tweaked suspension‑leg profiles – all aimed at cleaning up the airflow over and under the car. The result should be a stickier front end that holds the corner better and a more stable, aerodynamically efficient chassis, giving RB extra grip and confidence as the weekend’s high‑speed turns arrive.

Audi F1 Team.summary: Audi’s aero package has been overhauled – the entire front wing and nose now sit inside a sleek fairing, the front‑suspension covers have been reshaped, and the floor, diffuser and rear‑wing assembly are all fresh.  The new halo/engine‑cover fairings and re‑worked rear‑suspension covers also tidy up airflow and cooling.  All of these tweaks should give the car a cleaner aerodynamic surface, more stable down‑force and better tyre grip, giving Audi a stronger start and more confidence through the high‑speed corners this weekend.

Cadillac.summary: Cadillac has tweaked the front‑end aerodynamics – new brake‑cooling ducts keep the brakes from overheating, the suspension fairings now guide air more smoothly, and the diffuser’s winglet edge has been reshaped for a steadier rear‑downforce bite. These changes should give the car better grip and stability out of the corners, letting drivers push harder over the weekend’s sprint‑to‑finish.
